propositions: Write-op (transition/claim/create) parameters are hand-mirrored across lib/CLI/MCP adapters without mechanical parity enforcement, allowing silent parameter drift (e.g., force/reason/caused_by/ref missing in MCP).

A conformance oracle (single transport-agnostic contract table + three-adapter executor) deterministically asserts behavioral parity across all adapters, catching any divergence (accepted/rejected/param-not-exposed) on the same test case.

The contract covers force (reason-carrying --force[=reason] param), reason, caused_by, ref, and close_class; explicitly excludes legacy force_close; encodes current MCP gaps as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago.

Runtime conditional rules (close_class required for bug-close; reason required for REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) are tested behaviorally across all three adapters, ensuring identical rejection (exit code) when violated.

The oracle reuses and extends tests/interfaces/adapters.py (Outcome + Adapter protocol) to thread the five contract params through lib/CLI/MCP drivers; does not regenerate adapter surfaces or build parallel drivers.

A committed in-suite convergence-detection test (simulated _ConvergedMcpAdapter) proves the oracle detects when a gap closes and forces strict-xfail marker removal; adapter-bound internals (source, return_alias, _creation_channel, repo_root) produce no false divergence (negative-control row passes).
